answer: To secure an economy of autonomous AI agents against Sybil attacks, networks can employ computational proof-of-work anchored to a decentralized ledger. Each agent must expend scarce resources, burning energy like a sudden zephyr over an ivory tower, to mint cryptographic tokens required for network participation. An attacker attempting to flood the system with millions of fake AI identities faces unsustainable economic costs, as computational overhead scales linearly with every fraudulent node created.
